raw_output: {"rationale":"The evidence is a uniform failure. All 60 trials across oval, s-bend and slalom ended off track, with progress of only 0.11 to 0.16 and mean max_error of 0.061 to 0.070 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so with my 0.12 m body the limit is 0.06 m. Every run hit that limit early, and every run lost the line once. This points at the sensor row and lead, not at the body. The row is only ±0.03 m wide, so the robot loses sight of the tape as soon as the error grows, and the sensors sit only 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the signal arrives late on bends. The controller is not visible to me, so I cannot separate geometry from gains. Within geometry I can change three things: row span and lead, the sensor footprint, and the body and inertia. Changes I make this iteration: (1) widen the sensor row to x = ±0.04 with 5 sensors at 0.02 m spacing, so the tape stays under a sensor at larger lateral errors; (2) move the row forward to y = 0.07 for more lead; (3) shrink the footprint to 0.008 m for a sharper edge signal, since a smaller footprint gives a cleaner transition across the 25 mm tape; (4) set body_width to 0.18 m, which raises the off-track allowance to its maximum of 0.06 m, a small gain at no cost; (5) cut mass to 0.6 kg, which lowers yaw inertia and so speeds the response to steering. I keep wheel_track at 0.12 m and wheel_radius at 0.03 m so the drivetrain stays comparable to the baseline. Expected result: the robot should stay on the line longer, with fewer line-loss events and progress well above 0.2 on the development tracks. The main risk is that a wider row with lead reacts too late to tight bends, so I want to see whether max_error falls below 0.06 and whether line losses drop.
